questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why summers in the UK are getting shorter each year
How the daily weather forecasts are made on TV
How clouds cause dangerous heatwaves in Europe
How scientists use models to see how hot Earth may get
questions.why: They discuss how hot the planet could get and how scientists use climate models to find out.

questions.q: What record does Phil mention at the start?
options: The coldest winter in Europe
The highest June temperature in the UK
The longest heatwave ever recorded
The most rain in a single summer
questions.why: Phil says a new UK record for the highest June temperature was set at 37.7°C.

questions.q: What did the COP21 summit in 2015 agree to do?
options: Limit global warming to 1.5°C
Stop all greenhouse gas emissions by 2020
Build new supercomputers for climate research
Measure clouds around the world
questions.why: Phil says COP21 agreed to limit global warming to 1.5°C.

questions.q: How do climate models work, according to Pippa?
options: Scientists guess what the weather will be next year
Satellites take photos of what the future looks like
Data goes into supercomputers to show possible futures
Experts compare today's weather with old records
questions.why: She says physical and chemical data are fed into supercomputers, which paint pictures of possible futures.

questions.q: What does Kate Marvel say climate models produce?
options: Projections that depend on what humans do
Exact predictions of what will happen
Daily weather forecasts
Reports about past climates only
questions.why: She says models make projections, which are conditional: 'If we do this, then this will happen.'

questions.q: What does Kate say about the effect of clouds?
options: They only cool the planet
They have no real effect on the climate
They only appear in cold countries
They both cool the planet and warm it
questions.why: She says clouds cool the planet by blocking sunlight and warm it with their own greenhouse effect.

questions.q: What worries Phil about climate models?
options: They are too cheap to make and so not accurate
They seem complicated, as clouds keep changing
They are only used by scientists in the USA
They always seem to give people bad news
questions.why: Phil says models sound complicated and asks how you can monitor clouds that are always changing.

questions.q: What does Kate's final, more hopeful message suggest?
options: Global warming will slowly stop by itself
Scientists will no longer need climate models
Humans caused global warming, so they can fix it
Clouds will protect the planet from the heat
questions.why: Models show the problem is created by humans, so the solution is 'also in our hands'.
